entries.title: Do all readers start on the same side of a page?
entries.answer: English lines usually start on the left and go right. Hebrew and Arabic lines usually start on the right. Some scripts, such as traditional Mongolian, can be written in columns that run down the page. In some Japanese books the lines run down, and the next column is on the left. A reader learns where a line starts and which line comes next. In a book that mixes more than one script, some parts of the page can be read in a different direction from the parts around them.
facts: Even within a line read from right to left, a set of numerals can be written from left to right.

questions.text: How can tiny dots help someone read Hebrew?
Which vertical script puts the next column on the right?
How can a computer tell the different signs in a mixed line apart?

entries.title: How can a prefix or suffix change a word?
entries.answer: Some words have parts that help you guess the meaning. The beginning part in “rewrite” is re-, which often means again. The last part of “helpful” is -ful, which helps show that something gives or has help. English uses many parts that cannot stand alone as words. Looking for a familiar part may help you understand a new word, but the whole word often has a more specific meaning. Check how it is used in the sentence.
facts: A prefix comes at the beginning of a word or stem. A suffix comes at the end.

questions.text: What happens when each part can be a word on its own?
How are meaningful word parts different from beats in speech?
When might a whole expression mean more than its parts suggest?

entries.title: How can dots give readers extra clues in Hebrew?
entries.answer: Hebrew letters often give the reader the consonants in a word. Small signs called vowel points can fill in more of the sounds. Some of the signs sit below a letter, and others appear above or beside it. People can print them in books for beginners to help readers sound out words. Many everyday texts leave out the points, and readers use the letters, grammar, and meaning of the sentence to work out the words.
facts: Most Hebrew text is read from right to left, even when it includes vowel points.

questions.text: How do Arabic letters change shape as they join?
How does Devanagari show the vowels in a syllable?
How can readers tell which edge of a page to start at?

entries.title: How can Georgian writers make a headline stand out?
entries.answer: The curving letters you usually see in modern Georgian writing are called Mkhedruli. Writers can make a heading or a short phrase stand out by using forms called Mtavruli. Some of those forms rise to the same height, giving a line of text a more even top. In English, a capital letter can mark the start of a sentence. The Georgian headline style usually highlights an entire group of letters, so it works more like writing a sign in all capitals.
facts: Mkhedruli and Mtavruli are paired forms in Unicode, the system computers use to represent letters.

questions.text: How can two alphabets use a shape for different sounds?
In what directions can lines of writing run?
How do computers agree on the identity of a letter?

entries.title: How can people keep stories without writing them down?
entries.answer: People can pass on a story by telling it to someone who will tell it again. A repeated line, tune, or pattern can help a listener remember the next part. Families and communities pass along memories, poems, riddles, and other things this way. A teller may change some words to fit a new audience while keeping the main idea. Recordings and notes can help people share what a particular storyteller said.
facts: A story passed from speaker to listener can have more than one version.

questions.text: How can a few words stand for a bigger idea?
Why do old tales sometimes use animals that talk?
What kinds of traditions can people learn from each other?

entries.title: How can people learn in more than one language?
entries.answer: Some children speak one language at home and learn another in school or when they play with friends. Some classrooms use two or more languages to help students learn. For example, a student might first discuss an idea about plants in a language they know well, then learn the names for the parts of a plant in another language. Both can help the student explain the same idea in different settings.
facts: People can know different words in the languages they use because they speak them in different places.

questions.text: Why can people who speak one language sound different?
How can languages be related to one another?
How do stories and sayings help people use a language together?

entries.title: How can the same name be written in two scripts?
entries.answer: A reader who knows the Latin alphabet may have trouble reading a name written in a script they have never learned. A system for turning names into Latin letters is called romanization. A system can show how the original letters are written, how the name sounds, or some of both. Two systems can use different rules and give the same name different spellings. The original name can stay the same in its own script.
facts: The Latin alphabet used for English is one of many alphabets or scripts used around the world.

questions.text: How does Pinyin show the sound of words written in Chinese characters?
How does changing words into another language differ from changing letters?
How can familiar-looking letters make different sounds?

entries.title: How can two different languages be related?
entries.answer: Languages can change a little as people pass them on. Groups sometimes move apart and use language in different ways, generation after generation. After a long time, the groups may speak languages that no longer sound much alike. Linguists compare patterns in older words and sounds to look for shared beginnings. English, German, and Spanish are different languages in a large family called Indo-European. Comparing a whole pattern is more helpful than finding just one word that happens to sound alike.
facts: Two languages can be related even when someone who speaks one cannot understand the other.

questions.text: How can people use different varieties of the same language?
How can you break spoken words into smaller parts to compare them?
How did Chinese characters come to be used in Japanese writing?

entries.title: How can you count syllables in a word?
entries.answer: A syllable is one sound part of a spoken word. Say rainbow slowly and listen for two parts, rain and bow. If you clap once on each part, you clap twice. Frog has one syllable and dinosaur has three. A syllable usually has a vowel sound that you can hear, such as the long a sound in rain. Counting letters on the page will not tell you how many syllables you said. A word like cake has four letters but just one syllable.
facts: A spoken word can have one syllable or several syllables.
Different accents can change the number of syllables a speaker says in some words.

questions.text: How does an alphabet show the sounds in a word?
How are long and short sounds arranged in music?
What does a language use when its words are signed rather than spoken?

quiz.question: How many syllables do you hear in robot?
quiz.explanation: Say ro and bot separately. The word has two spoken parts.

entries.title: How could knots record numbers?
entries.answer: People in the Andes kept records using sets of cords called quipus. A main cord might hold many hanging cords. People could make different knots and put them at different heights. On some quipus, a knot’s position showed whether it counted ones, tens, or hundreds. Color and the way cords were grouped could add more information. Researchers can read numbers on many surviving quipus, but they are still learning what other features meant and how a trained reader used them.
facts: Some quipus have hundreds of cords, while others have far fewer.

questions.text: What kinds of supplies and work might an empire need to count?
How did a different culture make records with signs?
How can where a sign appears change the number it means?

entries.title: How did Maya writers put sounds and words into pictures?
entries.answer: Ancient Maya writing used signs called glyphs. A glyph might stand for a whole word, or it might stand for a sound like the beginning of a word. Different signs can fit into one block. Imagine solving a tiny puzzle in which the writer left clues about both the word and how to pronounce it. Maya artists wrote on stone, pottery, and in books. Some records describe when important events happened and who took part in them.
facts: Maya writing combined whole-word signs and signs for syllables.

questions.text: How could a writer give the date of an event?
How did Egyptian picture-like signs also stand for sounds?
What ancient signs are still waiting for a widely accepted reading?

entries.title: How did Sequoyah make a way to write Cherokee?
entries.answer: Sequoyah developed signs to write the Cherokee language. Most of the signs let a reader recognize a spoken syllable at a time. Instead of learning a different mark for every word, people could learn a group of signs and use them together to write many words. Some signs look like English letters, but that does not mean they have the same sounds. The Cherokee Nation teaches the system today and uses it in materials for Cherokee language learners.
facts: Sequoyah finished developing the Cherokee syllabary in 1821.

questions.text: How can you hear the beats in a spoken word?
Where else are signs for groups of sounds used?
How is an alphabet another way to represent spoken sounds?

entries.title: How did the Rosetta Stone help people read hieroglyphs?
entries.answer: The Rosetta Stone has the same announcement carved in three kinds of writing. One is in Greek, which scholars could already read. The other two use ancient Egyptian scripts, called hieroglyphs and Demotic. Comparing the parts gave scholars clues to the Egyptian signs. A royal name, for example, could help them make a guess about which signs represented its sounds. The stone is only part of a larger slab. Much of its upper section is missing, so there were gaps to work around.

sections.heading: A long puzzle
sections.text: In 1822, Jean-François Champollion announced a breakthrough in reading hieroglyphs. He built on work by several scholars, including Thomas Young.

facts: The announcement was made in 196 BCE.
The stone uses three scripts to write two languages.

questions.text: How can a picture of an owl help spell a word?
Why did many Egyptian settlements grow near the Nile?
How were early Mesopotamian records written?

quiz.question: Why was the Greek part useful to early readers of the Rosetta Stone?
options: It described how to make paper
It showed a map of Egypt
quiz.explanation: Scholars used the message they could read in Greek to look for patterns in the Egyptian writing.

entries.title: How do Arabic letters change shape in a word?
entries.answer: Arabic writing usually runs from right to left. Many letters join their neighbors, so a letter may look somewhat different at the beginning, middle, or end of a word. A few letters do not join to the next one in that direction. Dots help tell letters with similar shapes apart. Texts for learners may add marks for short vowels, while many familiar texts leave those marks out. The shared shapes still have patterns that readers learn to recognize.
facts: Artists have developed many styles of Arabic calligraphy.

questions.text: What jobs do the letters of an alphabet do?
How do Korean letters join into a different kind of group?
How did an older writing system use the position and shape of signs?

entries.title: How do Bangla letters show which vowel to say?
entries.answer: Bangla, also called Bengali, is often written with letters that show a consonant plus a usual vowel. A reader can see other vowel sounds marked around that letter in different places. Some signs reach around the letter on more than one side. A reader looks at the whole group before saying that part of the word. A group may also bring two consonants together, changing how their shapes appear on the page.
facts: This script is used for the Bangla language and also has forms used for other languages, including Assamese.

questions.text: How do added marks change a consonant’s usual vowel in Devanagari?
How do Korean sounds fit into blocks of letters?
How can a listener hear parts inside a word?

entries.title: How do Egyptian hieroglyphs work?
entries.answer: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs are signs used to write the Egyptian language. Some are easy to recognize as pictures, such as an owl or an eye. Their job still depends on where they appear in the writing. One sign can stand for a sound. Another can stand for a whole word. Some give a reader a clue about what kind of word appears nearby. A reader therefore needs to know the writing system to understand a line of signs, just as reading English takes more than recognizing a letter’s shape.
facts: In Egyptian hieroglyphs, an owl sign can represent the sound m.
Hieroglyphs appear in carved and painted inscriptions.

questions.text: How did one stone help people work out what the signs meant?
What were ancient Egyptian people’s towns and farms like?
How did another ancient writing system use marks in clay?

entries.title: How do people read braille?
entries.answer: Braille uses patterns of raised dots. A reader feels them with their fingertips. In six-dot braille, each space, called a cell, has room for six dots arranged in two columns. Which dots stick up tells the reader what the pattern means. Braille can represent letters, numbers, and other signs. In some versions, one pattern can stand for a whole word or a group of letters to save space. People use braille to read books, label things, and find their way around buildings.

sections.heading: Who invented it?
sections.text: Louis Braille developed the system as a young student in France. Before braille, some blind students learned to feel the shapes of raised print letters.

facts: A standard braille cell has room for six dots.
Braille is a way of writing and reading a language.

questions.text: What is an example of a language people can see instead of hear?
How do the familiar letters in a printed book work?
What other ways can a library help people read?

quiz.question: What part of a braille pattern can a reader feel?
quiz.explanation: The positions of raised dots tell the reader which pattern they are touching.

entries.title: How does a proverb say a lot in a few words?
entries.answer: A proverb is a short saying that people repeat to share an idea or some advice. For example, “Many hands make light work” tells us that a big job can feel easier when more people help. The saying talks about hands because it gives people a simple picture to remember. People may use a proverb at different times, and what counts as good advice can depend on what is happening.
facts: A proverb usually has a meaning people in a group recognize when they hear it.

questions.text: How do spoken sayings travel from one generation to the next?
How can a whole story with animals teach a lesson?
Why do people use different words for the same thing?

entries.title: How does American Sign Language work?
entries.answer: American Sign Language, or ASL, is a language that people can see. Signers use their hands, faces, and bodies to express ideas. A change in where or how a sign moves can matter, much as a change in sound can matter in a spoken language. ASL has its own grammar, the patterns people use to put ideas together. Some signs may look a little like what they mean, but people need to learn the language to understand a conversation.

sections.heading: Many sign languages
sections.text: ASL is used by many people in the United States and parts of Canada. British Sign Language is different, even though many hearing people in both places speak English.

facts: ASL is a natural language with rules of its own.
Signers can use their face and body to help express a question or idea.

questions.text: How do people use touch to read words?
What is an alphabet and what does each of its signs stand for?
Which country shares a border with the United States and has ASL users?

entries.title: What are some ways we see the Greek alphabet?
entries.answer: People use the Greek alphabet to write the Greek language. Its letters show sounds, just as English letters do, but the sets of letters are different. The Greek letter pi has a shape that looks a bit like a small table, and mathematicians use it to name a number connected to circles. That is an extra use of the sign. In a Greek word the same letter is part of the spelling and helps show how to say the word.
facts: Alpha and beta are the first two letters of the Greek alphabet.

questions.text: How is an alphabet different from other ways of writing?
What does pi tell us about every circle?
Which alphabet uses some letters whose shapes came from Greek?

entries.title: What can fingerspelling show in American Sign Language?
entries.answer: American Sign Language, or ASL, can use a series of handshapes to spell out letters of an English word. This is called fingerspelling. It can help show a name or a word that the people talking do not share a sign for. Signers use signs and grammar from ASL for most ideas. Fingerspelling is one part of this complete language.
facts: Other signed languages can have different ways of representing letters by hand.

questions.text: How can hands and faces work together in a full language?
Why do letters work together to spell a word?
Who can carry a message from a spoken language into a signed one?

entries.title: What do the small marks above and below Vietnamese letters do?
entries.answer: Vietnamese uses an alphabet with many letters that look familiar to English readers. Small marks can change the vowel itself or show its tone, which is the pattern of pitch as someone says the syllable. A letter can even have a vowel mark and a tone mark at the same time. A reader looks at those marks to decide how to say a word. Changing the tone can change which word a speaker means.
facts: Leaving out the tone mark can show the Vietnamese tone called ngang.

questions.text: How can Thai marks give clues to a spoken syllable?
Which Hawaiian marks tell a reader to stop briefly or hold a sound longer?
How can linguists write sounds more exactly than they are spelled?

entries.title: What does Pinyin tell a reader about a Mandarin word?
entries.answer: Pinyin is a system that uses Latin letters to help show how words are pronounced in Mandarin Chinese. Some marks over the letters can show what happens to the pitch of the voice on a syllable. The letters are a guide to sounds, so several Chinese characters may have the same Pinyin spelling and sound. Readers still use the Chinese characters and the rest of the sentence to work out the meaning.
facts: Libraries can use Pinyin forms of names and titles to help people find books written in Chinese.

questions.text: Why can one name have two spellings in Latin letters?
How do libraries keep track of a book’s author and title?
Why can a printed mark tell you about pitch?

entries.title: What happens when two words become one idea?
entries.answer: A compound combines two words to name one thing or idea. A “snowman” is a figure made of snow, and a “notebook” is a book for notes. You can often use what you know about the parts to guess the meaning. Still, you have to notice how the whole compound is used. A dragonfly is an insect, so the word does not mean a little dragon. Compounds may be written together, with a hyphen, or with a space between their parts.
facts: “Backpack” is a compound made from “back” and “pack.”

questions.text: How are compounds different from a word built with a prefix?
Why can a word made of two parts have more than two syllables?
What happens when the pieces of an expression do not tell you its meaning?

entries.title: What is an alphabet?
entries.answer: An alphabet is a set of letters used to write a language. In an alphabet, letters or groups of letters stand for sounds. This gives a writer a way to spell many words with a small set of signs. English uses 26 letters. The spelling does not always tell you which sound to make. In the word ship, for instance, s and h together stand for one sound. Other writing systems organize signs differently, and languages using the same alphabet can give its letters different jobs.
facts: English uses a form of the Latin alphabet.
A letter is a written mark. A sound is something you can say or hear.

questions.text: How can you hear the larger sound parts in a word?
What were some other jobs an ancient picture sign could do?
How can a reader feel letters and numbers without looking at them?

entries.title: What is the difference between translating and interpreting?
entries.answer: A translator works with writing in one language and makes a written version in another. An interpreter often works with words that are spoken or signed, such as during a class or a meeting. Both try to carry the message across, even when a saying does not make sense word for word in the other language. A translator can reread and change a sentence on paper. An interpreter may need to follow what is happening in real time.
facts: An interpreter can work between a spoken language and a signed language, or between two spoken languages.

questions.text: How does a signed language carry ideas?
Why can a saying mean more than the words taken one by one?
What changes if we only rewrite a name using another script?

entries.title: What were Indus seals?
entries.answer: Archaeologists have found small carved seals at ancient Indus sites. A seal has a design that can be pressed into soft material, leaving a mark. Many Indus seals show an animal and a short row of signs. The cuts are small enough that a careful craftsperson had to plan each design. Researchers have suggested different uses for the seals, including marking goods. Since there is no agreed way to read the signs, we still cannot say what most marks meant.
facts: Many known Indus seals were carved from a soft stone called steatite.

questions.text: Where were these seals found?
What gave researchers a way to read Egyptian signs?
What did early Chinese writers carve into bones?

entries.title: What were oracle bones used for?
entries.answer: During the Shang dynasty, people at the royal court asked questions about what might happen. A question could be about rain, crops, or a trip. They heated prepared animal bones or turtle shells until cracks appeared, then read the cracks for signs of an answer. Writers sometimes carved the question on the surface along with a date or result. Today the writing gives researchers a record of what people worried about and what signs they used to write Chinese.
facts: People made oracle bones from pieces such as cattle shoulder blades and turtle shells.

questions.text: What else have archaeologists found from Shang China?
How did Egyptian writers record a language using signs?
What happens when researchers cannot yet read an ancient set of signs?

entries.title: Where does the question mark go in Armenian?
entries.answer: An Armenian question mark is a small curved sign put above a vowel in the word that carries the question. It can point out which word asks for an answer. In an English sentence, we often put a question mark at the very end instead. A speaker can raise or change their voice on a word to make it sound like a question, and punctuation gives readers a clue about where that change happens.
facts: Armenian has its own alphabet as well as its own ways of placing punctuation.

questions.text: What are some other ways writing can sit on a page?
How can a sign help show the pitch of a syllable?
How do linguists write down exact sounds?

entries.title: Why can a written Thai vowel appear before the sound it follows?
entries.answer: Thai text normally runs from left to right. Vowels can be drawn around consonants, including to their left, right, above, or below. In some syllables, a marked vowel appears on the left, but the reader first says the consonant and then the vowel. Look at a whole group of signs to figure out how it fits together. This is one reason reading a script means learning more than the shapes of its letters.
facts: Some marks in Thai help show the pattern of pitch, called tone, used when a syllable is spoken.

questions.text: Does Devanagari also put some vowels before their letters?
How do Vietnamese readers know the pitch of a syllable?
Can a whole column of writing run downward?

entries.title: Why did people press signs into clay?
entries.answer: In ancient Mesopotamia, people used clay tablets as writing surfaces. A writer used a tool called a stylus to press small wedge shapes into soft clay. Groups of wedges formed signs in a system called cuneiform. Keeping track of food and other goods was one early use. People also wrote letters, stories, and math on tablets. A clay tablet could dry and become hard, allowing some messages to last for thousands of years. The marks often survive even when part of the tablet breaks.
facts: The earliest clay records used picture-like signs before wedge-shaped signs became common.
Ancient writers used cuneiform to record several languages, including Sumerian and Akkadian.

questions.text: What did another ancient writing system do with picture signs?
How did people work out the meaning of Egyptian signs?
Where can researchers find old records today?

entries.title: Why do Japanese readers learn three kinds of signs?
entries.answer: A sentence in Japanese can use three sets of signs. Kanji are characters that often help show the meaning of a word. Hiragana commonly marks particles, parts added to words, or words written without kanji. Katakana can show many words borrowed from outside Japan, or draw attention to a sound or name. Hiragana and katakana both represent short units of spoken Japanese. Learning how a sentence combines the three sets can help a reader see what belongs together.
facts: Kanji originally reached Japan from China.

questions.text: How does Korean form groups of letters for syllables?
Where else do signs represent units of spoken language?
How could Maya writers use more than one kind of sign?

entries.title: Why do Korean letters fit together in blocks?
entries.answer: Hangul is a way to write Korean. It has letters for sounds, but people arrange the letters in square-like groups. Each group represents a syllable, a small beat of speech. A syllable block can contain letters side by side and one below them. Grouping the letters helps a reader see how sounds fit together within the syllable. King Sejong helped introduce the writing system centuries ago so more people could learn a way of writing Korean.
facts: A book explaining the new writing system was published in 1446.

questions.text: How does Cherokee use individual signs for syllables?
What groups of signs appear together in Japanese writing?
How can you hear syllables without looking at written letters?

entries.title: Why do linguists write sounds with the IPA?
entries.answer: A word’s ordinary spelling does not always tell you how it sounds. In English, the letters “sh” work together in “ship” to spell one sound. The International Phonetic Alphabet has a separate sign for that sound. Linguists use such signs to describe speech, compare pronunciations, and write down sounds a reader might never have heard. A dictionary can use the signs to show how a word is said. Different pronunciations of one written word can get different descriptions.
facts: The IPA chart groups sounds partly by how and where we make them in the mouth or throat.

questions.text: Which words can have the same sounds even with different spelling?
Why can two groups of speakers pronounce the same word differently?
What do listeners notice when they hear words with several beats?

entries.title: Why do people use the same language in different ways?
entries.answer: A dialect is a form of a language used by a group of people. Their words, pronunciation, or ways of putting words together can differ from another group’s. One person might say “soda” where another says “pop.” People learn features from family, friends, books, and the places they spend time. A dialect has patterns its speakers learn, even when those patterns differ from the way a textbook speaks. Groups can share some features and differ in others.
facts: An accent describes pronunciation. A dialect can also differ in words or grammar.

questions.text: How can languages change far enough apart that they become different languages?
How can someone write down the difference in pronunciation?
Why can one pronunciation fit more than one word?

entries.title: Why do some words sound alike but mean different things?
entries.answer: Think of “pair” and “pear.” In many English accents, both words sound the same. One refers to two things and the other to a fruit. We can use the rest of the sentence to tell which word someone means. Spelling can help when we read, although some homophones are spelled alike too. Whether a pair counts as homophones can depend on the speaker’s accent. A sound difference in one place might disappear in another.
facts: “Sea” and “see” are another familiar pair of homophones in English.

questions.text: How can pronunciation change from one group to another?
How can people write a sound separately from its usual spelling?
What other clues can help people read unfamiliar words?

entries.title: Why do traditional Mongolian words run down a page?
entries.answer: Traditional Mongolian writing usually goes from the top of a column to the bottom. The next column goes to the right of the one just read. Many of its letters join their neighbors and look a little different at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end of a word. People can also write Mongolian with some other alphabets. A language and the script people choose to write it with are two different things.
facts: English books usually turn a line at the right edge, but a page of vertical Mongolian turns it at the bottom.

questions.text: How can vertical books differ from one another?
How can letters change shape when they join their neighbors?
How does an alphabet used for many languages work?

entries.title: Why do two small marks matter in Hawaiian writing?
entries.answer: Hawaiian has a letter called the ʻokina that shows a tiny stop in the voice. It is like the little stop between the two parts of “uh-oh.” The kahakō is a line over a vowel that tells the reader to hold the sound longer. These signs can help tell two words apart as well as show how to say them. That is why careful Hawaiian writing keeps them in people’s names and place names.
facts: The ʻokina is a letter. It can look like a small turned mark beside other letters.

questions.text: Why can a small sign change which Vietnamese word someone means?
How can readers keep a name’s sounds when writing it in a different alphabet?
How can a special alphabet help people record the sounds they hear?

entries.title: Why does a Devanagari letter sometimes come with a vowel sound?
entries.answer: Devanagari is a script used to write Hindi and several other languages. A letter for a consonant can come with a short vowel sound even when there is no separate vowel sign. To show another vowel in that part of a word, a writer can add a mark above, below, or beside the letter. Some marks also show that the usual vowel should be left out. You can often recognize words by the line along the tops of their letters.
facts: A vowel sign can be drawn before a consonant even when the vowel is heard after it.

questions.text: How does Bangla show when a vowel goes with a consonant?
What is a vowel point in Hebrew?
What makes a syllable different from a single sound?

entries.title: Why does an idiom mean more than its words say?
entries.answer: An idiom is an expression people know as a group of words. Its usual meaning can be different from what the words would describe on their own. If someone jokes that pigs can fly, the speaker probably thinks something is very unlikely. In another sentence, that same idea could be a story about a pig with wings. The surrounding words help us figure out which meaning makes sense. Idioms can change over time or be familiar to some groups and new to others.
facts: The expression about flying pigs has several forms in different places.

questions.text: When do parts of a word help explain what the word means?
How can a whole sentence help show which word someone means?
Why might an expression be familiar in one region and new in another?

entries.title: Why might a familiar-looking letter make a different sound in Cyrillic?
entries.answer: The Cyrillic alphabet is used for Russian and several other languages. Some letters look like letters in the alphabet used for English, but the matching shapes can stand for different sounds. A Cyrillic letter shaped like an English capital P often gives an R sound. Other Cyrillic letters, such as Ж, have shapes English readers may not recognize. A reader learns the sound rules of the language as well as the shapes of its letters.
facts: Bulgarians, Ukrainians, and other people who write with Cyrillic use some different letters from one another.

questions.text: What language uses the letters alpha and beta?
What makes a writing system an alphabet?
How can an alphabet show the sound of a name written in another script?
